subject: Decision Making
title: Consensus vs. Consent
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Consensus vs. Consent.

hook.text: Consensus means everyone agrees. Consent means no one objects. The difference is enormous in speed and quality.

buildup.text: Consensus seeks full agreement. It can take hours, days, or forever. One holdout blocks the entire group.

discovery.text: Consensus vs. Consent reveals the key principle behind better choices under uncertainty.

twist.text: Many organizations claim to use consensus but actually use consent. The practical difference determines meeting length.

climax.text: Consent is faster and often better. It avoids the watered-down compromise that true consensus frequently produces.

punchline.text: Not 'do you agree' but 'can you live with it?' Consent moves fast.

quiz.question: What is the difference between consensus and consent?
options: Consensus requires full agreement; consent requires no one objects enough to block
